title: Second-harmonic bounds give a fragile quadratic-response test in 14 Kepler quarters of KIC 10001893
abstract: We test a necessary second-harmonic amplitude relation for a steady instantaneous quadratic response to two fixed KIC 10001893 pulsations. We fit 14 public Kepler release-25 quarters. For early aperture flux, nominal conditional bounds put the difference amplitude above 21.39 ppm and the model cap at 20.43 ppm. Later bounds overlap. Removing one early quarter keeps separation in only 1 of 7 aperture-flux tests. All-data separation survives 9 of 14 removals. Thus the new amplitude test is fragile and does not robustly reject quadratic pulsation. It does not confirm a planet or find a new signal. Fixed frequencies, steady coefficients, source mixing and estimated noise coverage limit the result. Code, aggregate results, a figure, input hashes and separate-storage retrieval steps are included. External observations remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Nominal amplitude bounds and their change after one quarter is removed. Positive margins separate the bounds under the stated steady-model and noise assumptions.
